---
title: "Vendoring"
subtitle: "Copy the modules into your extension, pin them, and update them by hand."
description: "How to vendor quarto-lua-modules into a Quarto extension, declare them in _dependencies.yml, and update them to a new release."
toc: true
---

Quarto has no package manager for Lua.
An extension therefore keeps its own copy of each module it uses, under `_vendor/quarto-lua-modules/`, and commits that copy.
Readers of the extension never download anything when they render a document.

This page covers three things: placing the files, recording where they came from, and updating them.

## Place the files

Create `_vendor/quarto-lua-modules/` beside your filter, and copy the modules you use into it.
Each release attaches its modules as separate files, so you can fetch one module without the rest.

For a release, the files sit at:

```text
https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-lua-modules/releases/download/<version>/<file>
```

Copy the `LICENSE` too, from `quarto-lua-modules-<version>.tar.gz`, and keep it beside the copies.

### Copy the modules a module needs

A module can load another module from its own folder.
Copy the sibling with it, or the filter fails at render time with `module ... not found`.

| Module | Needs |
| --- | --- |
| `content-extraction.lua` | `string.lua`, `html.lua` |
| `html.lua` | `string.lua` |
| `metadata.lua` | `string.lua`, `logging.lua` |
| `paths.lua` | `string.lua` |
| `pandoc-helpers.lua` | `string.lua` |
| `schema-check.lua` | `string.lua`, `logging.lua` |
| `colour.lua`, `embedded.lua`, `git.lua`, `logging.lua`, `lookup.lua`, `string.lua` | nothing |

: Sibling modules each module loads. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[45,55]"}

### Load a module

Load each module with the path Quarto resolves inside a filter:

```lua
local str = require(quarto.utils.resolve_path('_vendor/quarto-lua-modules/string.lua'):gsub('%.lua$', ''))
```

## Declare the files in `_dependencies.yml`

Write a `_dependencies.yml` beside your `_extension.yml`.
It records the upstream, the version you took, and the checksum of each file.
Without it, nothing shows which release a copy came from, or whether it still matches.

```yaml
schema: 1
sources:
  quarto-lua-modules:
    origin: "https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-lua-modules"
    fetch: "{origin}/releases/download/{version}/{file}"
    version: "2.10.0"
    licence: MIT
    files:
      string.lua:
        sha256: "7801d2f217e803951313ef86f1f899cb6350a44cbb468b2d7c28dd6911a0fadc"
        runtime: any
```

Add one entry under `files` for each module you copy.

### Keys

| Key | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `schema` | Yes | The format version. Use `1`. |
| `sources` | Yes | The upstreams you vendor from, each under a short name. |
| `origin` | Yes | The upstream's home, such as its repository URL. |
| `fetch` | Yes | The URL of one file. It contains `{file}`, and may use `{origin}` and `{version}`. |
| `version` | Yes | The release every file below was taken from. |
| `licence` | Yes | The licence the upstream ships under, such as `MIT`. |
| `licence-url` | No | The URL of the licence file. Defaults to `{origin}/raw/{version}/LICENSE`. |
| `tag-prefix` | No | The text before the version in a release tag. Leave it out when the tag is the bare version, as it is here. |
| `files` | Yes | The files copied from this source, keyed by file name. A name holds no path. |
| `sha256` | Yes | The SHA-256 of the file exactly as it is in `_vendor/`. 64 hexadecimal characters. |
| `runtime` | No | `any`, which is the default, or `pandoc` for a file that needs a library only Pandoc provides. |

: Keys of `_dependencies.yml`. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[18,12,70]"}

The full schema is in the public [dependencies schema](https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-extension-test/blob/main/_extensions/extension-test/dependencies-schema.yml) of the `quarto-extension-test` repository.

## Verify the copies

Compare the checksum of each file with the value in `_dependencies.yml`.

```bash
shasum -a 256 _vendor/quarto-lua-modules/*.lua   # macOS
sha256sum _vendor/quarto-lua-modules/*.lua       # Linux
```

A mismatch means the file is not the one the manifest names.
Fetch it again from the release, or update the manifest if you meant to change the version.

## Update to a new release

1. Read the [changelog](changelog.qmd) from your version to the new one.
   A release can change a function you call, or a file another module now needs.
2. Download the files of the new release, and the `LICENSE`, from its release page.
3. Compute each file's checksum, as in [Verify the copies](#verify-the-copies).
4. Update `version` and each `sha256` in `_dependencies.yml`.
   Add an entry for any new file you now need, and remove the entry for any file you no longer copy.
5. Replace the files in `_vendor/quarto-lua-modules/`, and delete the ones you no longer use.
6. Render your extension's test documents, and check the output.
7. Commit the manifest and the `_vendor/` folder together.

Keep the version and the checksums in one commit, so that the history shows which release each copy came from.
